packages.label: גְּבוּרָה וְלֵב
packages.reason: The Torah opens with 'עִקַּר הַגְּבוּרָה בְּהַלֵּב' — the essence of gevurah IS the heart. Gevurah, the heart as its seat, conquering the evil inclination (אֵיזֶהוּ גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ), and Samson's feats are all presented as different expressions of the same underlying reality: inner strength rooted in the heart. The Rebbe uses 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת' twice to equate these concepts, marking them as parallel aspects of one domain. The conquering of the yetzer hara is not a result of gevurah (eitza) — it IS gevurah, i.e. the inner battle and the outer battle are the same thing from different angles.
